identity.title: A non-nucleotide activator reveals a second allosteric regulatory site in the type III CRISPR ribonuclease Csm6.

content.abstract: Type III CRISPR-Cas systems rely on cyclic oligoadenylate (cOA) signaling to activate ancillary nucleases such as Csm6, which serve as core effectors in antiviral immunity. While cOA-mediated Csm6 activation has been widely harnessed for molecular diagnostics, its broader application is constrained by inherent limitations, including poor cellular permeability and susceptibility to degradation by ring nucleases. Here, we conducted a high-throughput fluorescence-based screen and identified DMPCH (7,8-dimethyl-4-phenylchroman-2-one) as a non-nucleotide allosteric activator of Thermus thermophilus (Tt) Csm6. DMPCH selectively stimulates TtCsm6 ribonuclease activity by binding to the higher eukaryotes and prokaryotes nucleotide-binding domain dimerization interface, leading to expansion of the catalytic pocket and remodeling of the R-X4-6-H catalytic motif. Moreover, DMPCH acts synergistically with cA4 to activate TtCsm6, enabling rapid and sensitive RNA detection in a Cas13a-Csm6 system. Cell-based assays confirm that DMPCH activates TtCsm6 ribonuclease activity in live bacteria cells. When combined with DMPCH, an engineered miniCsm6 fused to pyocin S2 (PyS2) exerts potent and specific bactericidal activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Our work establishes a framework for discovering non-nucleotide activators of CRISPR-associated ribonucleases and highlights their potential as chemical tools in cell-based research and as therapeutic agents against bacterial pathogens.
